page: Microsoft Azure L12aos_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine deployment running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. It provides 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 6 physical cores utilizing two threads per core. Cache sizing comprises 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Modern vector operations are supported via AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16 instruction sets, alongside hardware cryptographic engines including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. System memory totals 96.0 GB, establishing an allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Discrete GPU hardware is not included.

A key feature of the L12aos_v4 is its bundled 8640 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, provisioned to serve high-volume local read and write operations. In benchmark evaluations, the instance delivers strong single-core performance, achieving upper-quartile scores in stress-ng single-core execution and Geekbench single-core metrics. Multi-threaded processing capabilities, reflected in multi-core Geekbench and PassMark CPU scores, place in the middle tier. Memory subsystem testing demonstrates standard cached read bandwidth of 912.02 GB/sec, while uncached large-block read operations register lower-tier throughput at 38.93 GB/sec, contrasted with average uncached write throughput at 27.56 GB/sec.

The hardware balance offers high local storage capacity per compute core, maximizing resource density for configurations constrained by disk footprint rather than pure CPU scaling. However, workloads requiring extreme multi-threaded parallelism or heavy uncached memory throughput face architectural constraints. This profile makes the instance well matched for transactional database systems, distributed NoSQL databases, search indexing, and real-time caching services that benefit from dense, high-capacity direct-attached NVMe storage.
description: Microsoft Azure L12aos_v4 is a storage-optimized instance powered by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system features 12 dedicated vCPUs across 6 physical cores, 96.0 GB of memory, and 8640 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, with no discrete GPU included. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong single-core compute performance supported by AVX-512 extensions, alongside average multi-core and database processing scores. While cached memory operations remain solid, uncached memory read bandwidth represents a relative performance bottleneck. With an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and direct-attached NVMe capacity, the L12aos_v4 offers an efficient hardware profile for disk-dense environments, making it suitable for transactional databases, NoSQL clusters, search engines, and data processing pipelines requiring rapid local storage access.
